prompt_edits: Add a mandatory step: recompute every ⌈x/y⌉ and ⌊x/y⌋ expression from its stated inputs and verify the ceiling/floor result. Two models found ceiling errors in Table 17-2 (37≠38, 74≠75) that two models missed.

Add a mandatory step: for every figure, visually inspect the rendered page and verify that figure content, caption, and surrounding prose are mutually consistent (units, labels, values, arrow directions, color semantics, scale accuracy). One model found numerous figure semantic errors (FIG-3.4-01 P0, FIG-7.5-01 missing factor of 2, FIG-15.1-01 missing key element, FIG-16.1-01 title-annotation contradiction) that three models missed.

Add a mandatory step: build a cross-chapter ledger of canonical values (host counts, costs, rates, concurrency, throughput, prefill peaks) and verify consistency across all chapters. Multiple models found the same value appearing differently in different chapters (e.g., 6.24M vs 26.28M req/mo, 56,500 vs 19,800 tok/s prefill peak, 10 rps vs 40 rps volume basis).

Add a mandatory canonical-value ledger pass before adjudication: every reused value must be traced to its operating point and denominator (initial vs whole-context KV, 10 rps vs 40 rps, per-token vs per-request, theoretical vs sustained). This would have caught the CH11-02 and CH25-01 false positives and the CH4-03/CH25-01 volume-basis issues.

Require figure findings to include a rendered crop or exact coordinates plus the exact caption span and the arithmetic chain from the figure's own labels. Without that, visual findings should default to NEEDS-VERIFICATION rather than P0/P1. This round contains many figure-only claims that cannot be adjudicated from text.

Add a unit/request-basis check to every numeric finding: write the dimensional chain (tokens, requests, per-1K-token, per-month, per-host, per-GPU) and test the benign reading before filing. This would have prevented the DeepSeek:CH16-01 unit-conversion false positive and forced clearer separation of per-request versus per-token costs.

Add a mandatory canonical ledger gate: before accepting any chapter number, require the reviewer to map it to a ledger entry for request volume, tokens/request, KV GB/request, host count, cost basis, and hours/month. Flag any value that cannot be traced to one ledger row, and treat cross-chapter reuse of the same label with different bases as P1.

Add a figure arithmetic and semantic gate: for every figure, extract all numeric labels, axis ticks, percentile markers, and operator glyphs; recompute each from the caption and prose; verify percentile consistency (e.g., 1% mass at 5 s implies p99 at or above 5 s), color/legend semantics, and that drawn operators match the intended math (e.g., + vs x).

Add domain-scope and event-accounting checks: (a) table rows must be explicitly scoped inference vs training, and optimizer/gradient terms in inference tables are P1; (b) prefix-cache ledgers must distinguish initial processing from reprocessing, with total processed under 100% reuse equal to initial plus appended, not initial per call; (c) cost claims must state per-host vs total, average vs peak, and per-1K-tokens vs per-request.

Fix the merge step before the next round: the consolidated register must carry the COMPLETE issue record (quoted_clause, observed, evidence/recomputation, root cause, correction, acceptance test) rather than a 300-character truncation, and each id must be globally unique in the form <MODEL>-<CH>-<NN>. The merge must also (a) mark cross-model duplicates as SAME-AS <id> instead of re-listing them under a UNIQUE tag, and (b) group findings by root cause with every anchor listed. In this round the truncation blocked adjudication of roughly half the entries, and at least 17 ids collided across COMMON and UNIQUE lists (CH4-01 twice within one model's own output, plus CH4-02, CH5-01, CH5-02, CH6-01, CH11-TTFT-SLO-01, CH15-01, CH16-01, CH17-02, CH20-01, CH22-01, CH24-01, CH25-01, FIG-3.4-01, FIG-6.2-01, FIG-11.1-GREEN, FIG-43-01), so the UNIQUE tags and the convergence counts in the register are not trustworthy.

Require every reviewer to maintain and cite a CANONICAL-VALUE LEDGER before filing any numeric finding, and to name the ledger entry the finding contradicts (with that entry's location) in the issue record. Minimum ledger entries: per-request KV bytes together with the request definition it belongs to (9.2K input vs 9.5K whole context); per-host KV budget; host prefill PEAK vs PLANNING rate and the MFU each assumes; monthly volume basis; the definition of the 8.6 s figure (time-in-system via Little's law vs service time); in-flight count; canonical host count and the utilisation policy each figure assumes; TTFT and end-to-end SLO values. Rationale: the highest-value defects this round (24.1 vs 24.9 vs 24.2 GB per request; 56,500 vs 19,800 tok/s, i.e. 100% vs 35% MFU; 6.24M vs 24.96M vs 25.92M requests/month; 21 vs 32 canonical hosts; 1.2 s vs 2 s TTFT SLO) are all ledger-level, and four models filed them under a dozen unrelated ids, so the merge could not see them as one root cause. Add a mandatory cross-check that every table row states its policy basis (full utilisation vs 70% x 95%) so that rows are comparable.

Add two mandatory fields to the finding template and one to the figure protocol. (a) 'operator and rounding bound': quote the operator (=, ~, approximately, <=, ceil/floor) and state the rounding bound implied by the printed precision, then state explicitly whether the finding survives if the operator is read as approximate (a ceiling is integer-valued and does not get that exemption). (b) 'alternative benign reading': name the alternative denominator, population, operating point, cache policy, SLO or illustrative scope under which the printed value is correct, and say why it fails; if a benign reading exists, downgrade rather than escalate. (c) For figure findings, require the exact recomputation from the figure's own printed numbers and a RENDER-VERIFIED flag that may only be set if the page was viewed at print size; unrendered figure findings must be filed as NEEDS-VERIFICATION with the check specified. Rationale: this round produced at least two misreads (the n = 1,000 zero-event confidence bound, where n = ln(0.05)/ln(1-0.003) = 997; and the $0.0208 per 1K-token-request unit equivalence) and one probable misread (239 tok/s decode rate, which is exactly 3.35 TB/s / 14 GB, i.e. a 7B FP16 model, not the canonical 70B), while roughly 20 figure findings could not be adjudicated at all without the render.
